messages:
Maya Patel: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — thanks for the roadmap clarity. pulling together the process questions that came up in the live q&a so leadership can answer one place.

Omar Singh: two quick ones: 1) release cadence — are we standardizing on weekly vs biweekly? 2) what quality bar gating looks like now (esp for infra/runtime changes).

Jess Carter: short answers: cadence is moving to a mixed model — infra/runtime teams keep weekly sprints for small patches; product feature teams default to biweekly releases unless they opt into weekly canaries.

Jess Carter: quality gate remains the same but we want clearer perf/regression thresholds in PRs. perf regressions >10% on benchmark keys should block.

Raul Gomez: oncall follow-up — per the trial, primary rotation is 1 week, secondary is 2 weeks (overlap handoff on Monday morning). documentation is here: https://redwood.example/docs/oncall (will add a date for the trial conclusion notes).

Ava Thompson: SLA question from a PM — what latency SLOs do we advertise for Dedicated plans and do we have automated fallbacks?

Jess Carter: Dedicated customers get an uptime SLA (99.9%) plus route-level p95 latency targets in their contracts. for general guidance: p95 <= 200ms for small seqs, p95 <= 500ms for long-context or non-accelerated models. automatic fallback is enabled for critical routes per policy (model variant/region).

Omar Singh: can we get a concise PR checklist to put in PR templates? got a couple of PRs that merged without perf measurements.

Jess Carter: yes — adding a checklist snippet here for the PR template, open to edits:
```
PR checklist:
- unit tests added/updated
- integration smoke + canary plan
- perf bench run (link to run) — regression < 10% on key metrics
- security review if touching auth/data paths
- rollout + rollback plan specified
```

Maya Patel: nice. can someone from infra/eng-sre confirm the perf metric names we want to gate on so product teams can automate bench runs?

Raul Gomez: will do. I'll share the bench script and metric names (qps, tail-latency-p95, memory-alloc) in eng-sre channel by EOD tomorrow.

DeployBot: new canary lane created by @Jess Carter for release/1723 — canary window 24h :rocket:

Ava Thompson: for the SLA language in customer-facing docs — can we make a short faq line about fallbacks and what customers should expect during regional capacity issues? customers asked in the q&a.

Jess Carter: good call — product + legal to draft a one-paragraph faq. Maya — want me to loop legal and PM?

Maya Patel: please do. also i'll host a 30-min office hours follow-up tomorrow 11am PT to answer leftover questions and collect any edge cases. agenda: release cadence examples, gated checklist, oncall handoff process, SLA FAQ.

Omar Singh: perfect — will bring the checklist PR draft.

Raul Gomez: adding a short runbook link in the office hours notes would help oncall handoffs.

Maya Patel: noted — will post notes + action items after the office hours. thanks all :thumbsup:
